When Calibration Fails the Vulnerable Hospital:
Federated Conformal Risk Control
via Risk-Curve Shrinkage

Nafis Fuad Shahid Affiliation: Dhaka, Bangladesh E-mail nafisfuadshahid@gmail.com
Abstract

Conformal risk control (CRC) provides distribution-free guarantees on segmentation quality by calibrating a prediction-set threshold on held-out data. In federated deployments, the standard approach pools calibration scores across sites into a single threshold. We provide the first quantification, on real multi-institutional brain tumor data (FeTS-2022, 1,251 subjects, 20 institutions), showing that this naive pooled CRC protects the average hospital but violates coverage at 40% of individual institutions, with the worst site exceeding the target false-negative rate by 7.8 percentage points. The naive alternative—per-site local CRC—largely restores coverage but inflates prediction sets by 83×83\times, rendering them clinically useless. We propose a shrinkage-based federated CRC protocol: each site transmits only its empirical risk curve (GG scalars) to a server, which computes a shrinkage-regularized threshold per site. A single hyperparameter n0n_{0} smoothly trades worst-case coverage for prediction-set efficiency; leave-one-site-out sensitivity analysis identifies n0=19n_{0}{=}19, achieving 2.7/20 violations at 2.0×2.0\times stretch. We further show that direct Lagrangian optimization of coverage budgets fails—concentrating risk on vulnerable hospitals—and that the finite-sample correction term is essential: removing it triples violations. The marginal CRC guarantee is preserved by construction under the stated site-mixture assumption; per-site coverage is validated across four targets with three seeds. No patient-level images, masks, or per-volume scores leave any site.

Keywords: 
Federated Learning Conformal Risk Control Segmentation Uncertainty Quantification

1 Introduction

Deploying segmentation models across hospitals requires calibrated uncertainty: clinicians must know when a model’s output can be trusted and when it cannot. Conformal risk control (CRC) [1] provides distribution-free, finite-sample guarantees of the form 𝔼⁡[ℓ⁡(Cλ​(X),Y)]≤α\mathbb{E}[\ell(C_{\lambda}(X),Y)]\leq\alpha, where ℓ\ell is a monotone loss and λ\lambda is calibrated on held-out data. CRC has been applied to centralized medical segmentation—morphological dilation families for brain lesions [10], conditional CRC [8], and semantic CRC with region-specific control [14]—but never in the federated setting where calibration data is distributed across heterogeneous institutions that cannot share patient data.

In federated learning (FL) [9], the natural approach pools calibration scores from all sites to compute a single global threshold, inheriting federated conformal prediction machinery [7]. We show this naive pooled CRC harbors a critical failure mode: it satisfies the marginal coverage guarantee (averaging over the site mixture) while violating coverage at individual institutions. On FeTS-2022 brain tumor data [12] with 20 real institutions, 40% of sites exceed the target α=0.10\alpha{=}0.10, with the worst reaching FNR=0.178{=}0.178. In radiation therapy planning, this means missed tumor voxels at specific hospitals—potentially leaving cancerous tissue untreated—while aggregate metrics suggest everything is calibrated. This marginal-vs-conditional coverage gap is well studied in conformal prediction theory [16, 4], but its magnitude in federated medical segmentation has not been quantified.

Contributions. (1) We provide the first quantification, on 1,251 real multi-institutional brain tumor volumes, of the marginal-conditional coverage gap for federated CRC, showing that 8/20 institutions fail coverage while the average appears well-calibrated. (2) We propose a shrinkage-based federated CRC protocol where each site transmits only its empirical risk curve (GG scalars), and a single hyperparameter n0n_{0} provides a principled coverage-efficiency dial validated via post-hoc sensitivity analysis. (3) We show that direct Lagrangian budget optimization fails, concentrating risk on vulnerable hospitals, and that the finite-sample correction term is essential—removing it triples violations to the level of naive pooling. (4) The marginal CRC guarantee is preserved by construction under the stated site-mixture assumption; per-site coverage is empirically near-nominal across all tested configurations.

2 Related Work

CRC for segmentation. Angelopoulos et al. [1] introduced CRC for monotone losses. Recent work extends it to centralized segmentation: morphological dilation families for brain lesions [10], conditional CRC [8], and semantic CRC with region-specific control [14]. All assume centralized calibration data.

Federated conformal prediction. Lu et al. [7] prove federated CP coverage under partial exchangeability for classification. Extensions address group-conditional [17], Byzantine-robust [6], privacy-preserving [13], and weighted-quantile [11] settings. All target scalar nonconformity scores for classification—none extend to pixel-level segmentation losses or CRC’s continuous threshold inversion. The cell federated ×\times CRC ×\times pixel-level segmentation is empty. Exact conditional coverage is impossible without structural assumptions [16, 4]; our per-site coverage is empirical, viewed as approximate group-conditional coverage where each “group” is a hospital.

Federated segmentation with uncertainty. FUNAvg [15] aggregates MC-dropout uncertainty; FedEvi [3] uses evidential learning. Neither provides formal coverage guarantees. FedStein [5] applies James–Stein shrinkage to FL model parameters; we apply shrinkage to empirical risk curves for post-hoc calibration—a complementary perspective.

3 Method

3.1 Setting

Consider KK sites with nkn_{k} calibration volumes (Xik,Yik)(X_{i}^{k},Y_{i}^{k}) each. A pre-trained model ff produces predicted probabilities via sigmoid activation. We define nested prediction sets Cλ​(X)={v:f​(X)v≥1−λ}C_{\lambda}(X)=\{v:f(X)_{v}\geq 1-\lambda\}, growing with λ\lambda. The per-volume false-negative rate ℓ⁡(Cλ,Y)=1−|Cλ∩Y|/|Y|\ell(C_{\lambda},Y)=1-|C_{\lambda}\cap Y|/|Y| is non-increasing in λ\lambda and bounded in [0,1][0,1], so B=1B=1 in the CRC correction [1]. Goal: find λ^\hat{\lambda} such that 𝔼⁡[ℓ⁡(Cλ^​(Xtest),Ytest)]≤α\mathbb{E}[\ell(C_{\hat{\lambda}}(X_{\mathrm{test}}),Y_{\mathrm{test}})]\leq\alpha.

3.2 Why Pooled CRC Fails

Centralized CRC [1] computes the empirical risk R^​(λ)=1n​∑iℓi​(λ)\hat{R}(\lambda)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i}\ell_{i}(\lambda) and sets λ^=inf{λ:R^​(λ)+B/(n+1)≤α}\hat{\lambda}=\inf\{\lambda:\hat{R}(\lambda)+B/(n{+}1)\leq\alpha\}. Naive pooled federated CRC pools all N=∑knkN=\sum_{k}n_{k} scores identically. Under partial exchangeability [7], this controls the marginal risk 𝔼⁡[ℓtest]≤α\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\mathrm{test}}]\leq\alpha but not site-conditional risk 𝔼⁡[ℓ∣H=k]\mathbb{E}[\ell\mid H{=}k]. When sites differ in tumor prevalence, scanner protocols, or difficulty, the pooled threshold is dominated by majority-site behavior, and minority sites can have 𝔼⁡[ℓ∣H=k]≫α\mathbb{E}[\ell\mid H{=}k]\gg\alpha.

3.3 Per-Site Local CRC and Its Cost

Each site independently sets λ^k=inf{λ:R^k​(λ)+B/(nk+1)≤α}\hat{\lambda}_{k}=\inf\{\lambda:\hat{R}_{k}(\lambda)+B/(n_{k}{+}1)\leq\alpha\}. This guarantees site-conditional coverage but, for small nkn_{k}, the correction B/(nk+1)B/(n_{k}{+}1) is prohibitively large. With nk=5n_{k}{=}5 and B=1B{=}1, the correction alone is 0.167>α=0.100.167>\alpha{=}0.10: the constraint becomes unsatisfiable, forcing λ^k=λmax\hat{\lambda}_{k}=\lambda_{\mathrm{max}} (predict everything as tumor) and stretch exceeding 80×80\times.

3.4 Shrinkage-Based Federated CRC

We propose an intermediate approach (Fig. 1). Each site computes its local empirical risk curve R^k​(λ)\hat{R}_{k}(\lambda) on a grid Λ={λ1,…,λG}\Lambda=\{\lambda_{1},\ldots,\lambda_{G}\} and transmits only this GG-dimensional vector to the server. The server computes R^global​(λ)=1N​∑knk​R^k​(λ)\hat{R}_{\mathrm{global}}(\lambda)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k}n_{k}\hat{R}_{k}(\lambda) and the shrinkage risk curve:

R^kshrink​(λ)=wk⋅R^k​(λ)+(1−wk)⋅R^global​(λ)+corrk,\hat{R}_{k}^{\mathrm{shrink}}(\lambda)=w_{k}\cdot\hat{R}_{k}(\lambda)+(1-w_{k})\cdot\hat{R}_{\mathrm{global}}(\lambda)+\mathrm{corr}_{k}, (1)

where wk=nk/(nk+n0)w_{k}=n_{k}/(n_{k}+n_{0}) is the shrinkage weight—the standard empirical Bayes form where n0n_{0} acts as prior precision [5]—and corrk=wk⋅B/(nk+1)+(1−wk)⋅B/(N+1)\mathrm{corr}_{k}=w_{k}\cdot B/(n_{k}{+}1)+(1{-}w_{k})\cdot B/(N{+}1) is a heuristic interpolation between the per-site and pooled finite-sample corrections, motivated by but not formally derived from CRC theory. The threshold is λ^kshrink=inf{λ∈Λ:R^kshrink​(λ)≤α}\hat{\lambda}_{k}^{\mathrm{shrink}}=\inf\{\lambda\in\Lambda:\hat{R}_{k}^{\mathrm{shrink}}(\lambda)\leq\alpha\}.

Behavior. n0→0n_{0}\to 0: recovers per-site CRC (high coverage, high stretch). n0→∞n_{0}\to\infty: recovers pooled CRC (low stretch, poor worst-site coverage). Intermediate n0n_{0} interpolates smoothly.

Privacy. Each site transmits GG real numbers summarizing aggregate loss statistics. No individual volumes, masks, or per-volume scores leave the site. Total bandwidth: ∼0.8{\sim}0.8 KB for G=200G{=}200.

3.5 Theoretical Guarantee

Theorem 3.1 (Site-Marginal Federated CRC)

Assume partial exchangeability: for each site kk, (Z1k,…,Znkk,Ztestk)(Z_{1}^{k},\ldots,Z_{n_{k}}^{k},Z_{\mathrm{test}}^{k}) is exchangeable given H=kH{=}k, with ℙ⁡(H=k)=(nk+1)/(N+K)\mathbb{P}(H{=}k)=(n_{k}{+}1)/(N{+}K). Define λ^fed=max⁡{λ^pool,maxk⁡λ^kshrink}\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{fed}}=\max\{\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{pool}},\,\max_{k}\hat{\lambda}_{k}^{\mathrm{shrink}}\}.
Then 𝔼⁡[ℓ⁡(Cλ^fed​(Xtest),Ytest)]≤α\mathbb{E}[\ell(C_{\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{fed}}}(X_{\mathrm{test}}),Y_{\mathrm{test}})]\leq\alpha.

Proof

Since λ^fed≥λ^pool\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{fed}}\geq\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{pool}} by construction and ℓ\ell is non-increasing in λ\lambda, we have ℓ⁡(Cλ^fed​(X),Y)≤ℓ⁡(Cλ^pool​(X),Y)\ell(C_{\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{fed}}}(X),Y)\leq\ell(C_{\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{pool}}}(X),Y) for all (X,Y)(X,Y). The pooled CRC threshold satisfies 𝔼⁡[ℓtest​(λ^pool)]≤α\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\mathrm{test}}(\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{pool}})]\leq\alpha via standard CRC inversion [1] extended across the site mixture using the tower property [7]. By monotonicity, 𝔼⁡[ℓtest​(λ^fed)]≤α\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\mathrm{test}}(\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{fed}})]\leq\alpha.

Remark (scope of guarantee). This marginal guarantee is inherited from pooled CRC via monotonicity under the stated site-mixture assumption—it holds for any choice of per-site thresholds, as long as the deployed threshold includes λ^pool\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{pool}} in the maximum. The value of shrinkage is therefore entirely empirical: the conservative global λ^fed\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{fed}} achieves 0 violations at n0=9n_{0}{=}9 but at 67×67\times stretch (Table 2), whereas per-site thresholds λ^kshrink\hat{\lambda}_{k}^{\mathrm{shrink}} yield practical stretch while maintaining near-nominal site-level coverage in all tested configurations. A site-conditional bound remains an open problem; exact conditional coverage is impossible without structural assumptions [16, 4]. CRC prediction sets are designed to contain the true mask; stretch (|Cλ^|/|Y||C_{\hat{\lambda}}|/|Y|) is the appropriate efficiency measure.

4 Experiments

4.1 Setup

Data. FeTS-2022 training set [12]: 1,251 multi-modal brain MRI volumes (T1, T1Gd, T2, FLAIR) from 23 institutions. We retain the 20 with ≥\geq6 subjects (range: 6–511). Volumes with no tumor voxels (|Y|=0|Y|{=}0) are excluded since FNR is undefined; no such cases occurred in our data. Per-site 50/50 cal/test splits with seeds {42,1337,2024}\{42,1337,2024\}; we report mean±\pmstd.

Model. Pre-trained SegResNet from the MONAI model zoo [2], trained on BraTS-2021. This simulates realistic deployment: a centrally pre-trained model calibrated locally.

CRC details. Loss: per-volume pixel-FNR. Prediction sets: Cλ={v:f​(X)v≥1−λ}C_{\lambda}=\{v:f(X)_{v}\geq 1-\lambda\} on G=200G{=}200 uniformly spaced λ∈[0,1]\lambda\in[0,1]. Monotonicity enforced via cumulative minimum over increasing λ\lambda; the uniform spacing induces discretization error <0.005{<}0.005 in λ\lambda. Target α=0.10\alpha=0.10, swept over {0.05,0.10,0.15,0.20}\{0.05,0.10,0.15,0.20\}.

Metrics. (i) Violations: sites with mean test FNR >α>\alpha. (ii) Worst-site FNR. (iii) Stretch: |Cλ^|/|Y||C_{\hat{\lambda}}|/|Y| (1×1\times = exact match to ground truth).

4.2 Main Results

Table 1 presents results across three seeds. The failure mode is stark: B3 achieves marginal FNR≈α\approx\alpha but violates coverage at 8.0±2.48.0\pm 2.4 of 20 sites, with the worst site reaching FNR =0.178=0.178—nearly double the target. B2 reduces violations to 1.31.3 but inflates stretch to 83×83\times, rendering predictions clinically useless.

Our method navigates this trade-off via n0n_{0}. At n0=9n_{0}{=}9: matches B2’s violations (1.31.3) while reducing stretch by 65% (83×83\times to 29×29\times). At n0=15n_{0}{=}15: stretch drops to 4.4×4.4\times with only 2.7 violations. Leave-one-site-out sensitivity analysis (Sec. 4.3) identifies n0=19n_{0}{=}19 as a favorable operating point, achieving the same violation count as n0=15n_{0}{=}15 at just 2.0×2.0\times stretch—a 97.5% reduction from B2. Critically, the failure is not a small-sample artifact: Fig. 2 shows that Institution 18 (382 patients, 30% of the dataset) is miscovered at FNR=0.150{=}0.150, and B2’s stretch explodes to 100−250×100{-}250\times at small sites while ours stays below 5×5\times.

4.3 The n0n_{0} Dial and LOSO Sensitivity Analysis

Fig. 3 shows how n0n_{0} controls the coverage-efficiency frontier. Small n0n_{0} (≤9\leq 9): few violations, high stretch (per-site CRC regime). Large n0n_{0} (≥30\geq 30): low stretch, many violations (pooled regime). The knee at n0∈[10,20]n_{0}\in[10,20] (shaded) offers the best trade-off.

As a post-hoc sensitivity analysis, we perform leave-one-site-out evaluation: for each candidate n0n_{0}, hold out one site, calibrate shrinkage on the remaining K−1K{-}1 sites’ calibration data, and evaluate violations and stretch on the held-out site. LOSO identifies n0=19n_{0}{=}19 as the lowest-stretch operating point with ≤\leq3 mean violations, achieving 2.7 violations at 2.0×2.0\times stretch—squarely within the sweet spot of Fig. 3. The failure mode persists across all tested α∈{0.05,0.10,0.15,0.20}\alpha\in\{0.05,0.10,0.15,0.20\}: B3 violates 5–8 sites at each target while ours (n0=9n_{0}{=}9) reduces violations to 0–1.

4.4 Why Direct Optimization Fails

Table 1 includes a budget allocation baseline that directly optimizes per-site thresholds. The formulation minimizes total stretch subject to a marginal risk constraint: min⁡∑kλ1,…,λK⁡Sk​(λk)\min_{\lambda_{1},\ldots,\lambda_{K}}\sum_{k}S_{k}(\lambda_{k}) s.t. ∑kpk​Lk​(λk)≤α\sum_{k}p_{k}L_{k}(\lambda_{k})\leq\alpha, where Lk​(λ)=R^k​(λ)+B/(nk+1)L_{k}(\lambda)=\hat{R}_{k}(\lambda)+B/(n_{k}{+}1), SkS_{k} is mean stretch at site kk, and pk=(nk+1)/(N+K)p_{k}=(n_{k}{+}1)/(N{+}K). For a given Lagrange multiplier μ\mu, each site selects λk​(μ)=arg⁡minλ∈Λ​[Sk​(λ)+μ⋅pk⋅Lk​(λ)]\lambda_{k}(\mu)=\arg\min_{\lambda\in\Lambda}[S_{k}(\lambda)+\mu\cdot p_{k}\cdot L_{k}(\lambda)]; we binary-search on μ\mu until the constraint binds.

Uncapped budget allocation achieves minimal stretch (1.4×1.4\times) but catastrophically fails 12.3/20 sites (worst FNR=0.351{=}0.351): the optimizer concentrates risk on small, hard institutions to satisfy the marginal constraint cheaply. Adding a per-site cap (maxk⁡Lk≤α+0.03\max_{k}L_{k}\leq\alpha+0.03) reduces violations to 2.7 but inflates stretch to 71.6×71.6\times—worse than shrinkage n0=9n_{0}{=}9 on both dimensions. Shrinkage uses a blended risk estimator that implicitly regularizes toward the global curve, an inductive bias the constrained optimizer cannot replicate.

4.5 Ablations and Sensitivity

Table 2 probes the method’s sensitivity along three axes.

The correction term corrk\mathrm{corr}_{k} is essential. Removing corrk\mathrm{corr}_{k} is catastrophic: violations jump from 1.3–2.7 to 8.0–9.3 across all n0n_{0} values, with worst FNR rising to 0.173–0.181—comparable to naive pooled CRC. corrk\mathrm{corr}_{k} interpolates between local and pooled CRC corrections; its formal finite-sample analysis is future work, but its empirical necessity is unambiguous.

Conservative λ^fed\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{fed}} (Theorem 3.1). Deploying the single global threshold λ^fed=max⁡{λ^pool,maxk⁡λ^kshrink}\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{fed}}=\max\{\hat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{pool}},\max_{k}\hat{\lambda}_{k}^{\mathrm{shrink}}\} dramatically reduces violations (0 at n0=9n_{0}{=}9) but at extreme stretch (67×67\times). This quantifies the gap between the formal guarantee and practical deployment, confirming that per-site thresholds are necessary for clinical utility.

Grid resolution GG. At n0=15n_{0}{=}15: G=50G{=}50 yields 35.7×35.7\times stretch (discretization too coarse); G=200G{=}200 and G=500G{=}500 yield 4.4×4.4\times and 3.0×3.0\times respectively with similar violations. G=200G{=}200 is a stable, practical choice.

5 Discussion

Clinical significance. Our results show naive federated calibration exposes specific hospitals to this risk—including Institution 18 (382 patients)—while appearing calibrated on average. Vulnerability here arises from case-mix and outcome heterogeneity across sites, not merely from small sample size: even our largest institution is miscovered under naive pooling.

Limitations. Theorem 3.1 provides only a marginal guarantee under the stated site-mixture assumption; the per-site deployment is empirically validated but formally open. If the test-site mixture differs from calibration-site proportions, the marginal guarantee may not transfer directly. We use a single pre-trained model on one dataset; validation with additional anatomies, backbones, and federally trained models is needed. Adapting federated conformal baselines such as FedWQ-CP [11] or group-conditional FCP [17] to pixel-level CRC is future work.

6 Conclusion

We quantified a failure mode of naive pooled federated calibration: on real multi-institutional brain tumor data, 40% of hospitals exceed the target false-negative rate while the average looks fine. Our shrinkage-based federated CRC protocol provides a principled, privacy-preserving dial between worst-case coverage and prediction-set efficiency, with n0n_{0} validated via leave-one-site-out sensitivity analysis. Direct optimization of coverage budgets fails by exploiting vulnerable hospitals; the finite-sample correction, though heuristic, is essential—removing it triples violations.
